hints: Count increasing subsequences ending at each value, grouped by their final value.
A subsequence ending at x can extend any increasing subsequence whose last value is strictly smaller than x.
A Fenwick tree over compressed values stores the number of subsequences for each value prefix.
analogy: For each item, extend every valid sequence ending with a smaller value and add the new one-item sequence.
example: For [1,2,1], the increasing subsequences are [1] at the first item, [2], [1,2], and [1] at the last item: total 4.
algorithm: Coordinate-compress values. At each x, ways=1+Fenwick.sum(rank-1); add ways at rank. Sum all ways modulo 1,000,000,007.
correctness: Every nonempty increasing subsequence has a unique final index; its earlier part is either empty or ends at a strictly smaller value, exactly what the prefix query counts.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
